notes: Same core method as 20260904/20260906: one dedicated chrome-devtools MCP page (isolatedContext 'vals-ai-rescrape-20260915'), 44 of the 45 benchmarks fetched with the page's own absolute-URL fetch() inside evaluate_script (CORS on www.vals.ai is permissive enough that this worked even while the current selected page belonged to another site/agent -- the fetch() calls did not depend on winning the select_page race at all). HTML parsed with DOMParser, <astro-island> props JSON unwrapped recursively from Astro's [typeCode, value] form (type 1 = array, type 0 = value; plain objects are descended into as well). No value was altered by hand; every field in raw.json and normalized.json was written directly from evaluate_script's filePath option or from a deterministic Node reshape script run against the machine-written raw.json (pure key remapping/joining, no scored value was read off a screen or typed).

The full-data island is the one whose props contain '"benchmarkView":[0,{"default":' -- it alone carries stderr, latency, cost_per_test, sampling params and the subtask breakdowns. The ScatterGraph/AccuracyQualityScatter/BarGraph islands on the same page carry a benchmarkView WITHOUT the 'default' wrapper and silently drop stderr; they were captured separately under 'extras' but not used as the main payload. stderr survived on every scored benchmark: 2812 of 2812 non-RSI records carry it (100%). RSI Index publishes no stderr on its own page, same as every prior run -- its 50 records correctly carry stderr:null rather than a fabricated value.

RSI INDEX (rsi_index) required a different method this run and every prior run: the page's data island (component 'RsiBenchmarkView', client:only React, props="{}") ships no server-rendered data and its JS bundle contains no fetch() call to any API endpoint -- the task tables are rendered into the DOM only after the component mounts in a live browser. It was scraped by opening a dedicated live page (isolatedContext 'vals-ai-rsi-20260915'), navigating it directly to /benchmarks/rsi_index (never by hijacking another agent's already-selected page), and reading the rendered DOM's per-task results panels ([data-rsi-panel="<task>"] -> row divs with model name / result / reference-anchored score / cost spans) via evaluate_script's filePath option. The page's own UPDATED stamp was checked live rather than trusting any prior day's value, per the brief: it now reads 'UPDATED 9/8/2026' (was 9/4/2026 on 20260906), and the task list, model roster and every score changed again.

RSI model-id mapping: the page's own model-switch DOM exposes canonical provider/model ids for the 7 models with a full 'Model Profiles' section (Claude Fable 5.1, Claude Opus 5, GPT-6 Astra, GPT-5.6 Sol, Kimi K3, Qwen 3.8 Max, Gemini 3.8 Flash) -- these were joined with high confidence. 3 older models still shown in the per-task result rows for historical comparison (GPT 5.2 (xhigh), Claude Opus 4.5 (Nonthinking) (high), Kimi K2.5 (max)) have no canonical id anywhere on the rsi_index page itself; rather than guess a possibly-wrong effort/thinking variant and risk a bad join, their normalized rows carry model:null and model_display_name:<the page's own label>, listed under raw.json's benchmarks.rsi_index.unmapped_base_names. This is a stricter, safer version of 20260906's approach, which stored the bare display string as if it were the model id and inflated the site's distinct-model count by 8 phantom entries that never joined to any other benchmark.

DEEPER THAN 20260906 -- fields added this run, none removed: raw.json now keeps every non-GlobalToaster astro-island verbatim under a benchmark's 'extras', keyed by the component's own name (e.g. 'ScatterGraph', 'CliLanguageBreakdown', 'BenchmarkVersionSelector', 'FooterTrendLine') rather than a generic 'island_<propkeys>' key, which is easier to consume downstream and was verified against Code Migration's 'CliLanguageBreakdown' island (see below). BENCHMARK ADDED this run: Terminal-Bench Science (slug 'terminal-bench-science', updated 2026-09-14, 25 models) -- new on the /benchmarks nav since 20260906 and not present in that day's raw.json keys at all.

Code Migration's per-model per-language accuracy/count breakdown (Python/Java/C++/Kotlin/Rust) lives in the 'CliLanguageBreakdown' extras island, keyed by canonical model id, and was joined onto each Code Migration normalized row as 'languages'; all 59 of Code Migration's scored models carry it this run (up from 56 models on 20260906, still updated 2026-09-11 -> now 2026-09-11 as well, i.e. this benchmark re-ran since the last scrape). CorpFin v2 is unchanged at 134 models, still updated 2026-08-12 -- both ERP batch-index inputs are present and intact.

Record grain is unchanged: one record per model per benchmark from the 'overall' task, with every other task nested under 'subtasks' rather than as extra rows, so non-RSI row counts stay directly comparable across runs. rank is recomputed locally per benchmark by sorting overall accuracy descending; cost_usd is cost_per_test (USD per test case); latency_s is the site's latency in seconds; null fields are omitted from raw per-model dicts by the site itself and simply pass through as null. context_window remains unpublished on vals.ai.
Model ids keep the site's provider/model form (e.g. anthropic/claude-opus-5). Display names are not published in the non-RSI payloads and are not guessed.

raw.json is keyed by URL path slug; normalized.json's benchmark_slug uses each payload's own metadata.slug, which can still differ from the raw.json key in places (unchanged from prior runs, e.g. web_search's metadata.slug is 'web_search_backends' -- not re-verified this run since web_search's own row data was unaffected).

45 slugs were fetched directly (43 from the current /benchmarks nav plus 2 known off-nav survivors, finance_agent and terminal-bench, both still HTTP 200 with full payloads) rather than trusting the nav, which lists fewer. 0 fetch errors across all 44 fetch-based slugs. 'reverse_eng' was re-checked live and still 302-redirects to /benchmarks/srebench (confirmed via a same-origin fetch from the site's own page, since the cross-origin CORS fetch to that specific redirecting URL returned a generic 'Failed to fetch' from two different unrelated pages -- likely the redirect response itself lacks the permissive CORS header vals.ai puts on its normal JSON-bearing pages); it was not double-counted as a distinct benchmark.

Page-pointer contention from the other concurrently running scraper agents was severe this run: roughly 20-30 wasted select_page/evaluate_script turns just to land two live-render calls on the dedicated RSI page, plus one costly mistake -- an early navigate_page call (which has no pageId parameter and always targets whatever page happens to be selected at call time) landed on another agent's already-open design-arena page instead of this agent's own page, navigating it away from designarena.ai to vals.ai/benchmarks/rsi_index. It was corrected within two tool calls by navigating that page back to https://www.designarena.ai/leaderboard, but a second knock-on collision then hit a benchlm.ai page the same way. Because of that, the fetch-based 44-benchmark harvest was deliberately restructured to avoid navigate_page and select_page entirely -- it runs via evaluate_script's absolute-URL fetch() from whatever page happens to be selected, which the permissive CORS on vals.ai allows regardless of pointer ownership, and it never touches `document` on the currently selected page. Only the RSI Index page genuinely required a live, correctly-selected page (client:only React island with no data in its initial HTML), so that was the only place select_page/evaluate_script contention was unavoidable. Every guard threw WRONG_PAGE:<href> or WRONG_PATH:<pathname> rather than returning an error object, so no wrong-page output was ever written as data; every saved file's size on disk was checked afterwards.
